# QS-CFW-4540-42 - Quality specification - flange blank CFW-4540-42 (4140)

Revision: Rev D  
Plant: P3  
Parts: CFW-4540-42

Scope
This quality specification defines acceptance criteria and inspection methods for flange blank CFW-4540-42 (4140) produced at Plant P3. It covers material hardness, bore dimensional tolerance, maximum forging gross weight, inspection sampling rationale, examples of acceptable and unacceptable conditions, and record retention requirements. This document applies to incoming forgings, in-process forgings, and final inspection prior to release to the machining cell.

Background and rationale
CFW-4540-42 is a medium alloy steel forging requiring controlled mechanical properties and dimensional accuracy to meet downstream machining and assembly processes. Hardness is controlled to ensure machinability and final part performance. Bore concentricity and diameter tolerance are critical to ensure fixture fit and subsequent machining stock. Maximum forging weight is specified to ensure safe handling, proper die fill, and to prevent equipment overload during forging and handling operations. Inspection methods are chosen to be practical on the shop floor and reproducible by qualified inspectors.

Requirements table
The table below lists the controlled characteristics and acceptance criteria for flange blank CFW-4540-42 (CFW-4540-42).

- Characteristic: Material hardness (as-quenched/tempered)
  - Requirement: The hardness range for flange blank CFW-4540-42 (CFW-4540-42) is 38-44 HRC.
  - Rationale: Ensures machinability and strength balance for downstream processing and service.

- Characteristic: Bore diameter
  - Requirement: The bore diameter tolerance for flange blank CFW-4540-42 (CFW-4540-42) is ±0.07 mm.
  - Rationale: Controls fit-up to fixtures and initial machining allowances; prevents excessive material removal or rework.

- Characteristic: Forging gross weight
  - Requirement: The maximum forging weight for flange blank CFW-4540-42 (CFW-4540-42) is 71.9 kg.
  - Rationale: Limits handling risk and ensures compatibility with handling and heating equipment capacities.

Inspection method
General approach
Inspections shall be performed by qualified personnel familiar with induction hardness testing, calibrated dimensional measurement instruments, and weighing equipment. Inspectors shall follow written procedures and record results on the indicated inspection form.

Hardness inspection
- Use a portable hardness tester suitable for Rockwell C measurements. Perform verification on calibrated reference blocks before use.
- Inspect hardness at a minimum of three locations representative of the forged web and flange area; avoid edge decarburized zones and through-hardened transitions. Document individual readings and compute the observed range for the part.
- Acceptance criterion: readings must fall within the hardness range specified above. If any reading falls outside the range, proceed to nonconformance handling.

Bore diameter inspection
- Measure bore diameter using calibrated bore gauges or inside micrometers appropriate for the bore size. Ensure measurement probes contact clean, cool surfaces free of scale.
- Take measurements at two axial positions and at orthogonal orientations to assess runout and local ovality; record each measurement and note the maximum deviation from nominal.
- Acceptance criterion: measured diameter must conform to the bore diameter tolerance specified above.

Weight verification
- Weigh the forging in its as-forged condition on a calibrated platform scale. Record the gross weight on the inspection record.
- Acceptance criterion: weight must not exceed the maximum forging weight specified above. If weight exceeds that value, follow nonconformance handling.

Examples and interpretation
- Example acceptable condition: hardness readings of values that lie within the specified hardness range across the sampled locations, bore measurements that stay within the specified bore tolerance, and weight under the maximum forging weight. Mark the part as acceptable and release to machining.
- Example reject condition: a single hardness reading above or below the specified hardness range indicates a process control failure in heat treatment or forging; do not release. Similarly, a bore measurement outside the specified tolerance indicates die wear or misalignment; initiate tooling evaluation. A part exceeding the maximum forging weight requires investigation for die overfill or incorrect preform and must be segregated.

Nonconformance handling
Segregation and immediate actions
- Any part failing to meet one or more requirements shall be segregated and labeled with a nonconformance tag. Do not release for machining.

Root cause and disposition
- Initiate a containment and root cause activity. Actions should include review of forging process records, die condition, material heat treatment records, and handling or heating cycle notes to identify the likely source of the nonconformance.
- Disposition options include rework, reheat treatment, machining scrap, or return to forging, subject to engineering approval and demonstration that the final part will meet customer and safety requirements. Document the chosen disposition and approval authority on the nonconformance record.

Records to keep
Maintain the following records for each lot or heat in accordance with plant document control procedures:
- Hardness test logs, including instrument verification, individual readings, and inspector signature.
- Dimensional inspection records for bore measurements, including instrument calibration references.
- Gross weight record from the platform scale, with scale identification and calibration reference.
- Nonconformance reports, root cause analysis notes, disposition decisions, and approvals.
- Process parameter logs relevant to forging and heat treatment when available.

Retention and audit
All records shall be retained and made available for internal and external audits as required by plant quality procedures. Records must include sufficient detail to reconstruct the inspection and disposition decisions.

Revision control
This is Revision Rev D of QS-CFW-4540-42. Changes to this specification must be processed through formal revision procedures at Plant P3.

Related documents
None.
